drhp.business: Avantel Limited designs, develops and manufactures strategic equipment for Indian Defence Forces and Government institutions, including Software Defined Radios (SDR), Wind Profiler Radar (WPR) systems, SATCOM Ground Station Systems, HF systems, MSS SATCOM terminals and Network Management Software Solutions. Its primary customers are DRDO, ISRO, Defence PSUs, shipyards, ordnance factories, Indian Railways and research institutes, alongside listed companies such as L&T and NewSpace India Limited. risks.note: Avantel operates predominantly in the strategic sector (Defence and other Government institutions), characterized by extended procurement timelines and complex acquisition processes, posing risks to timely order finalisation and execution.
risks.risk: Extended defence/government procurement timelines and complex acquisition processes

risks.note: An increasing number of new entrants have entered the sector, buoyed by the Government's 'Make in India' initiative, intensifying market competition and requiring Avantel to continuously strengthen technological capabilities and value proposition.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition from new entrants under 'Make in India'

risks.note: Global realignment of semiconductor manufacturing capacity toward high-performance computing and AI has intensified supply constraints for processors, memory modules and programmable logic devices critical to defense-grade systems; extended lead times and allocation-based supply present a material execution risk for programs with fixed delivery schedules.
risks.risk: Supply constraints in specialized electronic components

risks.note: The enhanced size of operations, coupled with addition of multiple production sites, has increased complexity in operations, talent acquisition and retention, supply chain management, financial management and customer support.
risks.risk: Operational complexity from scale-up and multi-site expansion

risks.note: The Company operates predominantly in the strategic Defence/Government sector, making it dependent on government procurement cycles and priorities.
risks.risk: Sector/customer concentration in Defence and Government institutions

risks.note: Evolving dynamics including entry of well-funded technology start-ups and potential shifts in government procurement priorities require continued strategic attention, even though the Company does not foresee threats materially impairing its current order book or near-term growth trajectory.

Subsidiary Imeds Global Private Limited has incurred losses due to significant R&D investment and rising employee/operational costs needed to build a product portfolio and secure regulatory approvals (e.g., pending certifications for Ventilators and Patient Monitoring Systems) in a highly regulated industry.
risks.risk: Execution risk in the new, regulated medical devices vertical (Imeds)
